root_cause.text: In the rocker worlds port teardown path, `rocker_world_port_post_fini()` incorrectly tied freeing the per-port `rocker_port->wpriv` allocation to the optional `wops->port_post_fini` callback, so configurations like `rocker_ofdpa_ops` with a NULL callback leaked the allocated port-private memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `rocker_world_port_post_fini()` from returning early on `!wops->port_post_fini` to only conditionally invoking the callback while always executing `kfree(rocker_port->wpriv);`, and the CVE states `rocker_world_port_pre_init()` allocates `rocker_port->wpriv` with `kzalloc(...)` but `rocker_ofdpa_ops` leaves `port_post_fini` NULL, causing the memory to never be freed.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `rocker_world_port_post_fini()` from returning early on `!wops->port_post_fini` to only conditionally invoking the callback while always executing `kfree(rocker_port->wpriv);`, and the CVE states `rocker_world_port_pre_init()` allocates `rocker_port->wpriv` with `kzalloc(...)` but `rocker_ofdpa_ops` leaves `port_post_fini` NULL, causing the memory to never be freed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure rocker_world_port_post_fini always frees rocker_port->wpriv while only invoking port_post_fini when the callback is present.
intent_record.what: The code removes the early return when wops->port_post_fini is NULL and rewrites the conditional so that wops->port_post_fini(rocker_port) is called only if the callback exists, while leaving the subsequent kfree(rocker_port->wpriv) unconditionally executed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, rocker_port->wpriv is now always freed during rocker_world_port_post_fini(), even when the optional port_post_fini callback is absent. This prevents the function from exiting early and skipping cleanup of the private world data.

grouping_result.intent: Ensure rocker_world_port_post_fini always frees rocker_port->wpriv while only invoking port_post_fini when the callback is present.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by decoupling freeing rocker_port->wpriv from the optional wops->port_post_fini callback, ensuring the per-port private memory is always freed even when the callback is NULL.

candidates.rationale: This conditional gates the teardown path on the optional callback's presence, which is the root cause because it incorrectly ties later cleanup of rocker_port->wpriv to whether port_post_fini exists.
This early return causes the function to exit before freeing rocker_port->wpriv when wops->port_post_fini is NULL, directly producing the memory leak.

vuln_statements.explanation: This early return exits rocker_world_port_post_fini() before freeing rocker_port->wpriv when wops->port_post_fini is NULL, directly causing the per-port private memory leak described in the root cause.

This conditional incorrectly makes the teardown path depend on the optional port_post_fini callback, leading to the early exit path where rocker_port->wpriv is not freed for configurations with a NULL callback.

    ops hooks which each world can implement in world-specific way.
    Also introduce world infrastructure along with OF-DPA world stub.
    
    Signed-off-by: Jiri Pirko <jiri@mellanox.com>
    Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant teardown logic is fully visible in the snippet. In `rocker_world_port_pre_init()`, per-port private memory is always allocated with `rocker_port->wpriv = kzalloc(wops->port_priv_size, GFP_KERNEL);`. However, in `rocker_world_port_post_fini()`, freeing that allocation is incorrectly made conditional on the optional callback: `if (!wops->port_post_fini) return;` followed only afterward by `wops->port_post_fini(rocker_port);` and `kfree(rocker_port->wpriv);`. This means if a world implementation has `wops->port_post_fini == NULL`, the function returns before `kfree(rocker_port->wpriv)`, leaking the per-port allocation. The fix would require freeing `rocker_port->wpriv` regardless of whether `port_post_fini` exists, but that is not present here.
